# helpers4 release

> GitHub Action (and reusable workflow) that releases JS/TS packages with a signed release commit created through the API on no branch, a tag used as a lock, a tarball built once, attested and published to npm with OIDC trusted publishing. It needs no GitHub App and no secret, and never writes to the release branch.

Use `helpers4/action-release@v0` with `mode: build` in a job that runs your code (`contents: read`), then `mode: publish` in a second job that can write and sign. For simple projects, the reusable workflow `helpers4/action-release/.github/workflows/release.yml@v0` wraps both jobs in one call. `mode: check` runs the version-independent checks in pull requests.

## Key facts

- The build job has `contents: read` only and runs your code; the publish job has `contents: write`, `id-token: write`, `attestations: write` and runs none of it.
- Version is computed from the last `v*` tag of the line and Conventional Commits (`bump: auto | patch | minor | major | alpha | beta | rc | resume`). Before 1.0.0 a `feat` is a patch and a breaking change a minor.
- The branch keeps a placeholder version (`0.0.0-development`); the real version lives in the release commit and the tag.
- A failed publication leaves the tag and a draft Release; rerun with `bump: resume` to publish the same tarball.
- Targets: `npm`, `none` (tag and Release only). The first npm publish of a package is manual (bootstrap).

- [action.yml](action.yml): inputs and outputs
- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): conventions for contributing to this action
